before.text: Reading an FR, TR, TEST or mapping through REST, the typed client or the REPL reports the creation and update times stored with that record. A read never reports the time of the read; when the store holds no time, the value is null (operator 2026-11-02: "This HAS to be fixed."; PR 87 slice P). A stored time written without an offset is read as UTC (operator 2026-11-02: "UTC"; pre-HV what-if finding: no contract row pinned it). A read never fills a missing date from the clock: a stored value without a complete date (a time alone, or a partial date) reads as null and is ignored when a mapping's creation time is chosen (operator 2026-11-02: "Strengthen 5 ACs, fix all 8 (Recommended)"; hostile validation finding R9-F4).

A readable stored time states its year, its month and its day as date components: a year and month alone, and year digits that appear only in a time, a fraction or another component, read as null and are ignored when a mapping's creation time is chosen, whatever the read clock says (hostile validation round 10 finding R10-F1; strengthened between rounds under the operator's "Strengthening Acceptance Criteria should always be the recommended option" and "don't gate on me between rounds", 2026-11-03).

before.text: Generated test artifacts are written only to test-owned disposable output locations, not to repository fixture or documentation paths. The location is compared with the checkout by path segment under the path's own syntax: a Windows-form path (a drive letter or a backslash) ignores case, drive letter included, and a POSIX path compares ordinally; a case alias of the checkout or of a folder inside it is refused, and a distinct sibling is accepted (operator 2026-11-02: "Strengthen 5 ACs, fix all 8 (Recommended)"; hostile validation finding R9-F3).

before.text: A test-owned temporary QBrain.AI instance uses the database inside its owned root: no inherited setting, in configuration or the process environment and in the canonical (QBrainAi, QBRAINAI_), legacy (Mcp, MCP_) or host-prefixed (DOTNET_, ASPNETCORE_) form, nor a connection-string or content-root variable, selects another database for it (a connection string, a data source, a database provider or an instance name), and a database selection outside the owned root is refused. Every consumer of a temporary instance takes its workspace, marker and server address from that instance, and no inherited setting overrides them. These are the unit-proved rules TR-MCP-NUKE-019 AC-6 relies on (operator 2026-10-29: "Strengthen ACs, fix both (Recommended)", "Run the 2 classes, AC first (Recommended)" and "Lane ACs (Recommended)"; operator 2026-10-30: "FR-MCP-TESTRESOURCE-001 (Recommended)"; hostile validation findings R8B-F2 and R8B-F3; holistic review findings PLAN-6, PLAN-7, RINT-1, RINT-2 and RINT-3). A REPL host started for a temporary instance names both a workspace and a marker, each strictly inside the instance's owned root, compared by path segment with either separator under the path's own syntax (a Windows-form path ignores case, drive letter included; a POSIX path compares ordinally; operator 2026-11-02: "Strengthen 5 ACs, fix all 8 (Recommended)", the sibling of hostile validation finding R9-F3) and with no '.' or '..' segment; the checkout's marker, another or sibling root, a parent-segment escape, the root itself as the marker, and a missing argument or value are refused (operator 2026-10-26: "if you surface new AC, add them without waiting for approval"; the start-argument rows of TemporaryInstanceChecksTests already prove it).

Unit tests are for FR, Integration tests are for TR."). A unit test that checks a recorded time (an auth rotation, a selection or a session transition) takes the clock values from test-owned scripted inputs and asserts them exactly; it never compares with the current time, never sleeps to separate two times, and its result cannot change with elapsed time, scheduling delay or a change to the system clock (hostile validation round 10 finding R10-F3; strengthened between rounds under the operator's "Strengthening Acceptance Criteria should always be the recommended option" and "don't gate on me between rounds", 2026-11-03). This covers every recorded time a unit test checks, including the creation and update times a service stamps on a record it stores: the test supplies the service's clock as scripted times and asserts that each stamp equals the scripted time the service read (sibling sweep before round 11 of hostile validation round 10 finding R10-F3, 2026-11-03, under the same rulings). A wall-clock bound is an assertion whose outcome depends on how much real time passes: an elapsed time compared with a limit, or work the test expects to have happened during a short real-time wait (for example a periodic tick, a file-system event or a debounce); such a test is an integration test. A timeout whose only effect is to fail a test that would otherwise hang, set far above the time the awaited step needs, is not a wall-clock bound (holistic read before round 11, 2026-11-03, under the same rulings).
